Plate 5 (cones) gave [25.00, 25.34]; plate 6 (cylinders) gave (19.91, 30.48); H2 (16-gon prisms with a bicone head, spans 6-24 mm, terminal heights 5.7-26.8 mm) gives (25.00, 36.00). The area law is confirmed in location; it is not sharpened, because the H2 ladder steps 25.00 -> 36.00 in one jump (1.44x) with nothing in between.

WHAT THE AREA LAW DOES NOT PREDICT: the three head losses at X = 9.00 (V22, V32, BX50). At 9.00 the area law says survive by a factor of ~2.8 on ratio, and the same-plate r=0.30 rung at X=25.00 kept every head. These three are the only outcomes on the plate that no monotone law reaches.

(2) PERMANENT SET (outcome `permanently_bent`). Confined entirely to r <= 0.30. 0/45 specimens at r >= 0.50 bent; 6-7 of 11 at r=0.30 bent; the r=0.25 columns bent as well ('present though bent'). Within r=0.30 the split is perfectly ordered by measured head-top height, threshold in (11.24, 14.75) mm: intact at z_top 6.99 (Y11, X11), 8.75 (V11), 11.24 (Y21, X21); bent at 14.75 (V21), 15.48 (Y31, X31), 19.72 (Y41, X41), 26.75 (V41). Expressed for engineering use without committing to a mechanism: at r=0.30 a vertical member survived 6 mm of free span and took permanent set at 12 mm; a 45-degree member survived 12 mm and took permanent set at 18 mm.

MODE ORDERING is monotone in section with no inversions: r >= 0.50 intact -> r = 0.30 bent, head retained -> r = 0.25 bent AND head lost. That is a single load axis acting on a shrinking cross-section, and it is why conclusion 2 (below) holds for 73 of 76 IDs.

ONE MECHANISM? Yes for 73 of 76. The S1 vertical bends (V21, V31, V41), the S2/S3 inclined bends (Y31, Y41, X31, X41), and the CM head losses all sit on one consistent picture: an area-law junction failure above X ~ 25-36, plus a bending/permanent-set mode that switches on at r <= 0.30 once the terminal is above ~13 mm. The inclined pattern differs from the vertical pattern by exactly one span rung, in the direction predicted by BOTH candidate mechanisms (lower terminal height, and sqrt(2) more cured area per layer at 45 degrees). NO for V22, V32 and BX50, which require a separate cause - a localised process event, a scoring/labelling error, or an unmodelled variance source inside the design-allowable band.

DISCOUNTING T01: JUSTIFIED, high confidence. The reported failure is of the assembly scaffold (two left-most edge support pillars plus the outer guard pillar), not of the tile-support interface the cell exists to measure, and the roof came down as a consequence. T02 carries the identical 0.2 mm nominal contact radius and survived. The tile is also not a load-ladder cell at all: I measured it as a 12.0 x 8.0 mm slab with its ~96 mm^2 down-facing underside at z = 10.70 and its top at z = 13.50, supported by an uncharacterised number of pillars - so its X is neither computable from the manifest nor comparable to the ladder. Score it under a new `scaffold_failed` code and exclude it from every physics reading.

DISCOUNTING BX50: NOT justified on the evidence as it stands; recommend scoring it as a specimen failure with a written, argued, attributable exclusion note rather than a silent drop. The failure mode reported ('head not attached to support') is a specimen outcome, not a scaffold outcome; the S4 outer guard mast failure is a separate, adjacent event. The plate-edge hypothesis is refuted as an X-axis effect by the edge analysis already on record: V11, Y11, X11 and X12 all sit at exactly x = -90.0, the same distance from the -X limit as T01 and closer than BX50, and all four are present_intact. What BX50 shares with T01 is strip_order 1 - outermost member of a rear assembly, adjacent to the most cantilevered tall feature on the plate - which is a scaffold-design correlate, not a specimen-physics one. plate-06-results.md section 6 is the governing precedent: an override of a pre-registered scoring rule is admissible only because it is written down, argued and attributable.

WHAT BY50's SURVIVAL IMPLIES - and this is the decisive new fact: BX50 and BY50 are geometrically IDENTICAL in the printed mesh. I measured both from home-support-calibration-HOME-CAL-S4-BRACED-model.stl: head rings 4.4086 mm^2 at d=2.400 (z=18.25), 0.7653 at d=1.000 (z=19.50), 6.8883 at d=3.000 (z=20.75); shaft 32 triangles, 0.7653 mm^2 at both z=0 and z=19.5. Identical to four decimal places, identical triangle counts, and the manifest gives angle_from_vertical_deg = 0.0 for every S4 specimen so neither leans. The `orientation` label is built into the mesh only for the BRACED cells - I confirmed BX51's brace lens extends in Y while BY51's extends in X - and has NO geometric expression for the brace=none cells that carry the anomaly.

Consequences: (a) BX50 vs BY50 is not an orientation contrast and must never be reported as one; it is a 1-vs-1 positional replicate of the same part. (b) The S4 design intended to cross orientation x radius x brace, but the orientation factor was not built for a third of the cells - that is a generator/manifest defect to file. (c) Since the two parts are the same part, the only remaining explanations for one losing its head at X = 9.00 while the other did not are plate position, local scaffold state, or run-to-run scatter. With n = 1 the pair establishes exactly one thing, and it is the safety-relevant thing: at X = 9.00, inside the engine's X_ALLOWED = 12 envelope, the outcome on this printer is NOT deterministic. That unmodelled variance, not the edge, is what the next plate has to bound.

STRUCTURAL CONFOUNDS THAT CANNOT BE BROKEN ON THIS PLATE: Y position is constant within each strip, so any Y effect is perfectly aliased with 'which assembly'; free span is perfectly aliased with terminal height because all 76 bases sit at z = 1.50; and strip_order 1 is aliased with proximity to the outermost guard mast in every strip.

THE 16-GON VERSUS CIRCLE MISMATCH BETWEEN ENGINE AND PLATE. The engine's tension and deflection laws assume circular sections (pi r^2, I = pi r^4/4); the plate builds 16-gons (area 3.0615 r^2, 2.5% low; I is ~3% low). Every X realised on this plate is 2.5% above its circular-section nominal, and every deflection is ~3% larger than the engine's model. Negligible at present precision, but it is a systematic bias in the direction of the plate being slightly weaker than the engine thinks, and it should be stated once rather than discovered later.
